title: Philippine Nation-Building & Indigenous Science and Technology
subject: Science, Technology, and Society
description: Pre-colonial, Spanish, American, and Post-colonial S&T history in the Philippines, DOST mandates and programs, Outstanding Filipino Scientists, and Indigenous Knowledge Systems.
sourceFile: STS-WK1-MTWThF A book reference in STS.pdf, STS MIDTERM REVIEWER.docx

questions.question: What complicated pre-colonial engineering feat in the Cordilleras demonstrates early Filipinos' ingenuity in surviving cold mountain terrain?
options: Concrete suspension highways
Hand-built rice terraces incorporating an elaborate irrigation system using water from forests and mountaintops
Coal-fired steam locomotives
Steel suspension bridges
questions.answer: Hand-built rice terraces incorporating an elaborate irrigation system using water from forests and mountaintops
questions.explanation: The Cordillera Rice Terraces remain functional today as a testament to indigenous engineering and environmental adaptation.

questions.question: Which scientific practices did early pre-colonial Filipinos already apply before Spanish colonization?
options: Using medicinal plants/herbs, farming and animal-raising, and terrestrial and maritime transportation
Satellite weather forecasting and genetic splicing
Petroleum refining and nuclear power
Electric jeepneys and microprocessors
questions.answer: Using medicinal plants/herbs, farming and animal-raising, and terrestrial and maritime transportation
questions.explanation: Pre-colonial communities possessed practical folk and indigenous science tailored to daily survival and local ecology.

questions.question: How did Spanish colonization alter science, education, and infrastructure in the Philippines?
options: It dismantled all stone structures and banned universities

It introduced Western science via the Galleon Trade, founded the University of Santo Tomas (offering medicine, pharmacy, etc.), and built stone walls, roads, bridges, and sanitation mainly for the principalia
It immediately established DOST and PAGASA
It secularized all public schools under Act No. 74
questions.answer: It introduced Western science via the Galleon Trade, founded the University of Santo Tomas (offering medicine, pharmacy, etc.), and built stone walls, roads, bridges, and sanitation mainly for the principalia
questions.explanation: Spanish colonial infrastructure and higher education at UST laid early Western academic foundations, though access was largely limited to the principalia.

questions.question: What major educational and scientific institutions did the American occupation establish to modernize Philippine S&T?
options: Secularized public education (Act No. 74 of 1901), Philippine Normal School (now PNU), and the Bureau of Science
The University of Santo Tomas and Galleon Trade
PAGASA and the Philippine Science High School
The Balik Scientist Program and eJeepney
questions.answer: Secularized public education (Act No. 74 of 1901), Philippine Normal School (now PNU), and the Bureau of Science
questions.explanation: The American era institutionalized public teacher training and national scientific research through the Bureau of Science.

questions.question: Which key scientific agencies were created or strengthened during President Ferdinand Marcos's administration?
options: Bureau of Science and UST
PAGASA (replacing the Weather Bureau), NAST (National Academy of Science and Technology), and NSTA (reconstituted from the 1958 NSDB, now DOST)
Cartagena Protocol and CERN
Philippine Normal School and Rotary Club
questions.answer: PAGASA (replacing the Weather Bureau), NAST (National Academy of Science and Technology), and NSTA (reconstituted from the 1958 NSDB, now DOST)
questions.explanation: Marcos expanded national S&T institutions, recognizing science and technology as vital drivers of nation-building.

questions.question: Under Executive Order No. 128 (1987), which department serves as the Philippines' premier agency mandated to lead and coordinate S&T efforts for economic and social benefit?
options: Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
Department of Science and Technology (DOST)
National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA)
Commission on Higher Education (CHED)
questions.answer: Department of Science and Technology (DOST)
questions.explanation: EO 128 elevated NSTA into the cabinet-level DOST, pursuing an 11-point S&T agenda.

questions.question: What is the goal of the Philippines' 'Balik Scientist Program'?
options: To send all high school students abroad permanently
To incentivize foreign-based Filipino scientists and experts to return and contribute to local R&D
To replace science teachers with AI chatbots
To privatize PAGASA weather stations
questions.answer: To incentivize foreign-based Filipino scientists and experts to return and contribute to local R&D
questions.explanation: The Balik Scientist Program counters brain drain by bringing Filipino experts home to strengthen local research and mentorship.

questions.question: Which specialized Philippine public educational initiatives nurture gifted youth in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM)?
options: Philippine Science High School System (PSHSS) and Special Science Elementary Schools (SSES)
Galleon Trade Academy and Bureau of Customs
Kattukong Craft Guilds only
Sarswela and Senakulo troupes
questions.answer: Philippine Science High School System (PSHSS) and Special Science Elementary Schools (SSES)
questions.explanation: PSHSS, SSES, STEM scholarships, and the K to 12 Spiral Progression build national scientific human capital.

questions.question: Why does the government establish Science & Technology (S&T) Parks alongside National Science & Engineering Complexes (such as at UP Diliman)?
options: To replace farmland with shopping malls
To foster collaboration and partnerships between academic researchers and industry
To ban foreign technology transfers
To serve as tourist theme parks
questions.answer: To foster collaboration and partnerships between academic researchers and industry
questions.explanation: S&T Parks connect university innovation directly with industrial commercialization and national development.

questions.question: Which of the 10 Outstanding Filipino Scientists (cited by Dr. Queena Lee-Chua, 2000) is renowned for mango flowering and tissue culture research?
options: Ramon Barba
Rafael Guerrero III
Josefino Comiso
Enrique Ostrea Jr.
questions.answer: Ramon Barba
questions.explanation: Ramon Barba revolutionized Philippine mango production through flower induction and tissue culture research.

questions.question: Who among the Outstanding Filipino Scientists pioneered tilapia sex-reversal culture research, greatly boosting aquaculture?
options: Lourdes Cruz
Rafael Guerrero III
Fabian Dayrit
Gregory Tangonan
questions.answer: Rafael Guerrero III
questions.explanation: Rafael Guerrero III developed practical tilapia sex-reversal techniques for Philippine fisheries.

questions.question: Dr. Lourdes Cruz gained international recognition for her biochemical research on:
options: Satellite imagery of Antarctica
Sea snail venom (conotoxins)
Graph theory in mathematics
Meconium newborn drug testing
questions.answer: Sea snail venom (conotoxins)
questions.explanation: Lourdes Cruz's pioneering work on Conus sea snail venom (conotoxins) advanced neuroscience and pharmacology.

questions.question: Match the Filipino scientist to their contribution: Josefino Comiso, Enrique Ostrea Jr., and Fabian Dayrit.
options: Comiso: Antarctica satellite imagery; Ostrea Jr.: meconium drug testing; Dayrit: herbal medicine (lagundi, coconut oil)
Comiso: mango tissue culture; Ostrea Jr.: tilapia sex reversal; Dayrit: IEEE electrical leadership
Comiso: plant biotech; Ostrea Jr.: graph theory; Dayrit: communications tech
Comiso: bamboo incubator; Ostrea Jr.: SALt lamp; Dayrit: eJeepney
questions.answer: Comiso: Antarctica satellite imagery; Ostrea Jr.: meconium drug testing; Dayrit: herbal medicine (lagundi, coconut oil)
questions.explanation: Each scientist represents Philippine excellence across earth observation, pediatrics/diagnostics, and natural products chemistry.

questions.question: Match the remaining Outstanding Filipino Scientists: Jose Cruz Jr., Lilian Patena, Mari-jo Ruiz, and Gregory Tangonan.
options: Cruz Jr.: Electrical engineering/IEEE; Patena: Plant biotechnology; Ruiz: Graph theory & math education; Tangonan: Communications technology
Cruz Jr.: Conotoxins; Patena: Herbal medicine; Ruiz: Antarctica satellites; Tangonan: Tilapia culture
Cruz Jr.: Pediatrics; Patena: Saltwater lamps; Ruiz: Flood tricycles; Tangonan: Dengue traps
Cruz Jr.: Astronomy; Patena: Civil law; Ruiz: Painting; Tangonan: Architecture
questions.answer: Cruz Jr.: Electrical engineering/IEEE; Patena: Plant biotechnology; Ruiz: Graph theory & math education; Tangonan: Communications technology
questions.explanation: All ten scientists listed by Queena Lee-Chua (2000) demonstrate world-class Filipino research across diverse fields.

questions.question: According to the Midterm Reviewer, how does S&T contribute to Philippine nation-building and citizens' quality of life?
options: It ensures national isolation from global research
It helps establish cohesive national goals (Alesina & Reich, 2015), solves modern problems, and supports a 'matatag, maginhawa at panatag na buhay'
It eliminates all traditional indigenous practices
It focuses exclusively on luxury consumer imports
questions.answer: It helps establish cohesive national goals (Alesina & Reich, 2015), solves modern problems, and supports a 'matatag, maginhawa at panatag na buhay'
questions.explanation: S&T empowers informed decision-making and fosters national self-reliance and resilience.

questions.question: How is an Indigenous Knowledge System preserved and transmitted across generations in Philippine communities?
options: Through corporate patents and encrypted cloud servers
Embedded in daily community life and passed down by elders through cultural practices, life stories, songs, and poems
Strictly via American colonial textbooks
Through standardized international SAT exams
questions.answer: Embedded in daily community life and passed down by elders through cultural practices, life stories, songs, and poems
questions.explanation: Indigenous knowledge lives in community traditions, oral storytelling, and everyday environmental practices.

questions.question: What is the relationship between an Indigenous Knowledge System and Indigenous Science?
options: They are completely unrelated opposites.
Indigenous science is a subset of the indigenous knowledge system—comprising complex knowledge, expertise, and practices guiding human interaction with the natural environment.
Indigenous science rejects all observation of nature.
Indigenous knowledge system is strictly modern AI software.
questions.answer: Indigenous science is a subset of the indigenous knowledge system—comprising complex knowledge, expertise, and practices guiding human interaction with the natural environment.
questions.explanation: Indigenous science encompasses empirical community practices built from generations of observing local ecosystems.

questions.question: Which of the following is an authentic example of Philippine indigenous science?
options: Predicting weather and seasons by observing animal behaviors and celestial patterns
Synthesizing plastics in petrochemical refineries
Launching geostationary weather satellites
Running CRISPR gene-editing clinics
questions.answer: Predicting weather and seasons by observing animal behaviors and celestial patterns
questions.explanation: Indigenous communities forecast weather, preserve food (salting, drying, fermentation), select seeds, use herbal medicine, and manage irrigation.

questions.question: Which list accurately captures additional Philippine indigenous S&T practices from Unit 3?
options: Food preservation (salting, drying, fermentation), classifying flora/fauna/soil types, seed selection, indigenous irrigation, and fruit wine/juice production
Steam engines, Gutenberg presses, and nuclear submarines
Kerosene refining and telegraphy
Digital 3D printing and blockchain
questions.answer: Food preservation (salting, drying, fermentation), classifying flora/fauna/soil types, seed selection, indigenous irrigation, and fruit wine/juice production
questions.explanation: These practices show systematic observation, classification, preservation, and sustainable resource management.

questions.question: How do innovations like Dr. Fe del Mundo's bamboo incubator and Aisa Mijeno's SALt lamp illustrate the integration of indigenous/local resources with modern S&T?
options: They use scarce, expensive European materials
They creatively adapt abundant local materials and contexts to produce low-cost, ethical, accessible scientific solutions
They ignore rural community needs entirely
They depend on diesel generators
questions.answer: They creatively adapt abundant local materials and contexts to produce low-cost, ethical, accessible scientific solutions
questions.explanation: Filipino ingenuity bridges local materials and modern scientific principles to solve pressing community challenges.

questions.question: In the 2006 Outstanding Young Scientists roster cited in Unit 2, which fields are represented by Rhodora Aldemita/Glenn Gregorio and Ma. Alicia Aguinaldo/Christina Binag respectively?
options: Biology and Chemistry
Astronomy and Architecture
Mechanical Engineering and Law
Geology and Oceanography
questions.answer: Biology and Chemistry
questions.explanation: Aldemita and Gregorio were recognized in biology, Aguinaldo and Binag in chemistry, alongside scholars like Queena Lee-Chua and Dindo Campilan.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'K to 12 Spiral Progression' approach in Philippine science education?
options: To teach science only in Grade 12
To integrate and revisit science concepts progressively with increasing depth across grade levels
To remove laboratory experiments from schools
To focus exclusively on foreign languages
questions.answer: To integrate and revisit science concepts progressively with increasing depth across grade levels
questions.explanation: Spiral progression builds foundational concepts early and deepens scientific literacy systematically across grades.

questions.question: What was the precursor agency created in 1958 that was later reconstituted into NSTA under Marcos and eventually became DOST?
options: National Science and Development Board (NSDB)
Philippine Atmospheric Agency (PAA)
Bureau of Plant Industry
Department of Public Works
questions.answer: National Science and Development Board (NSDB)
questions.explanation: Established in 1958 as NSDB, it became NSTA under Marcos and DOST under EO 128 in 1987.

questions.question: Besides her non-electric bamboo incubator, which pediatric breakthroughs are credited to Dr. Fe del Mundo?
options: Immunization advocacy, jaundice treatment, and the BRAT diet for curing diarrhea
Inventing the first compound microscope and penicillin
Mapping the Antarctic ice sheet
Developing Golden Rice
questions.answer: Immunization advocacy, jaundice treatment, and the BRAT diet for curing diarrhea
questions.explanation: Dr. Fe del Mundo transformed Filipino pediatric care through accessible innovations and public health research.

questions.question: How did the focus of public education and science differ between the Spanish and American periods in the Philippines?
options: Spanish era education/sanitation largely benefited the principalia and church-run colleges (like UST), whereas the American era secularized public schooling (Act No. 74) and founded the Bureau of Science
Spanish era banned all churches; American era banned public schools
Spanish era created DOST; American era created the Cordillera rice terraces
There was no difference in educational policy
questions.answer: Spanish era education/sanitation largely benefited the principalia and church-run colleges (like UST), whereas the American era secularized public schooling (Act No. 74) and founded the Bureau of Science
questions.explanation: Each colonial era left distinct institutional legacies that shaped Philippine S&T.

questions.question: How do indigenous Philippine communities classify plants, animals, and soil types?
options: Randomly without names
Based on cultural properties, ecological utility, and lived environmental observation
Only by Latin binomial names invented in Europe
Strictly by industrial market price
questions.answer: Based on cultural properties, ecological utility, and lived environmental observation
questions.explanation: Indigenous taxonomy connects ecological traits with practical farming, medicine, and cultural meaning.

questions.question: Why did President Ferdinand Marcos replace the older Weather Bureau with PAGASA?
options: To eliminate meteorology from government
To strengthen geophysical, atmospheric, and astronomical monitoring as part of national S&T modernization
To transfer weather tracking to private shipping firms
To focus only on mining operations
questions.answer: To strengthen geophysical, atmospheric, and astronomical monitoring as part of national S&T modernization
questions.explanation: Establishing PAGASA, NAST, and NSTA aimed to institutionalize modern scientific capacity in the Philippines.

questions.question: Which DOST initiatives directly support researchers, students, and patent development in the Philippines?
options: R&D funding grants for projects/patents and undergraduate/graduate STEM scholarships
Prohibiting Filipino students from entering universities
Taxing scientific publications
Eliminating engineering programs
questions.answer: R&D funding grants for projects/patents and undergraduate/graduate STEM scholarships
questions.explanation: Funding grants, scholarships, and S&T complexes work together to cultivate local talent and innovation.

questions.question: How do the Cordillera rice terraces prevent water scarcity and sustain mountain agriculture?
options: Through electric water pumps powered by coal
Through an integrated gravity irrigation system channeling water from mountain forests and peaks down through stepped terraces
By importing bottled water daily
By growing crops only during typhoons
questions.answer: Through an integrated gravity irrigation system channeling water from mountain forests and peaks down through stepped terraces
questions.explanation: Forest-fed irrigation and terraced stonework transform steep mountainsides into productive sustainable farms.

questions.question: Why is science education considered vital to Philippine nation-building?
options: It trains skilled professionals who foster national self-reliance and solve local challenges ethically
It guarantees everyone becomes a politician
It removes the need for agriculture and healthcare
It replaces cultural identity with foreign trends
questions.answer: It trains skilled professionals who foster national self-reliance and solve local challenges ethically
questions.explanation: Strong science education builds domestic capability to tackle public health, disaster resilience, and economic development.
